## Context / Problem
After an MCP blue-green cutover, `gate_status` on the new container reports a job that is still running on the draining container as `failed / daemon-stopped`, and writes that into the shared index. Callers then start a duplicate, billable gate run.

### Observation (read-only, 2026-11-18 PST)
Two occurrences on 2026-11-16, both on `sarcastic-specified-kodiakbear` (times UTC):
- `verify_completion_start` returned job `1794871413492186335-b6a138…` at 23:23:33. Autodeploy cut `/mcp` over to a new container (8093) at 23:23:27 and retired `rebar-mcp-b4e0d01b6491-8092` with `docker stop --time 1260` (graceful drain). At 23:24:36, `gate_status` returned `status: failed, verdict: daemon-stopped`. The index file then ended `passed / PASS`, written 23:25:36 by the draining container's daemon.
- `review_plan_start` returned job `1794872550672894186-492f05…` at 23:42:30. Cutover to 8092 came at 23:44:25. At 23:49:37, `gate_status` returned `failed / daemon-stopped`. The index ended `passed / PASS` at 23:51:57.
The caller acted on the false failure and started a duplicate, billable run each time (23:24:45 and 23:49:58).

### Mechanism (from code)
`_running_record_is_stale` (`src/rebar/llm/gate_runs.py:293`) treats a `running` index record as crashed whenever `_mcp_inflight.is_job_active(job_id)` (`src/rebar/_mcp_inflight.py:135`) is false. That registry lives in process memory. Both containers share the `.rebar/gate_runs` index on the `gerrit_mcp_code` volume, so the new container has no registry entry for the old container's job. `_materialize_stale_running` (`gate_runs.py:308`) then writes `failed` into the shared index, and the old daemon overwrites it later. Autodeploy keeps the old container draining for up to 1,260 s, so every gate that spans a cutover takes this path.

## Approach
Give each job an owner lock that the kernel releases when the owning process dies, and have the poller ask the lock instead of only its own memory.
1. Owner side (`src/rebar/_mcp_llm.py`, `_start_gate_job` at :257 and `_spawn_gate_daemon` at :218): the leader opens `.rebar/gate_runs/<job_id>.lock` and takes `rebar._store.lock_kernel.take_exclusive` (`lock_kernel.py:120`; `fcntl.flock` on POSIX, `msvcrt.locking` on Windows) before it writes the `running` record. The daemon's `finally` writes the terminal record first, then closes the fd and best-effort deletes the lock file. If the lock cannot be taken, the job still runs and pollers fall back to today's rule.
2. Poller side (`gate_runs.py`): a new helper `_owner_lock_held(job_id, repo_root)` opens the existing lock file without creating it and tries `take_exclusive`; `is_contention` (`lock_kernel.py:185`) means a live owner holds it. `_running_record_is_stale` returns False when the owner lock is held. A missing lock file, or a lock that can be taken, keeps today's behaviour (stale after the grace window). `_materialize_stale_running` already re-reads the record, so an owner that finishes between the probe and the write still wins.
Why a kernel lock: the two containers have separate PID namespaces, so a stamped PID cannot be checked across them, but `flock` is held on the shared inode under one kernel and is dropped when the holder dies. The store write lock relies on the same property (`lock_kernel.py` docstring). A heartbeat would need a time threshold; the lock needs none.
The owner-lock suffix is the literal `.lock` (`_OWNER_LOCK_SUFFIX`, `src/rebar/llm/gate_runs.py:106`). Its census key `lock::.lock` is already in `.github/mechanism-baseline.json:606`, so `python scripts/check_mechanism_delta.py --check` stays green without a marker. No `# mechanism-ok` marker is added: one naming this ticket would make `close_precheck._refuse_open_sunset_marker` (`src/rebar/_commands/close_precheck.py:554-562`) refuse this ticket's close. No config key, env var or flag.
Portability: `lock_kernel` already provides both legs, and paths use `pathlib`; the test helper process is started with `sys.executable` and pipes, no signals or `fork`.

## Scope
- `src/rebar/llm/gate_runs.py`: owner-lock helpers, `_running_record_is_stale`.
- `src/rebar/_mcp_llm.py`: take and release the owner lock.
- `tests/unit/test_mcp_gate_async.py`: regression tests.

## Testing
- Live owner in another process: a helper Python process (started with `sys.executable`) takes the owner lock for job `J`; the test writes a `running` record for `J` older than the grace window with an empty in-process registry; `gate_run_status(J)` returns `running` and the index file is unchanged.
- Owner died: the same helper exits (stdin closed), then `gate_run_status(J)` returns `failed / daemon-stopped` (existing tests for records with no lock file stay green).
- End to end: a `review_plan_start` with a blocking stub leaves `<job_id>.lock` held while running and released after the terminal record is written.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [x] A regression test simulates a job whose `running` index record was written by another process that is still alive, and asserts `gate_status` does not report `failed` or overwrite the index while that owner is live; `pytest tests/unit/test_mcp_gate_async.py` passes.
- [x] A job whose owning process really died is still materialized as failed (existing behaviour kept, test kept green).
- [x] `python scripts/check_mechanism_delta.py --check` exits 0 and `make verify` passes.
- [ ] After merge, the `sweep (windows)` job of `test.yml` on main passes.
